description: Place any number of Tiles (Panels and Notes, by id) on a Workspace's grid in one call: x and w in 12 columns, y and h in rows of 8 px at the user's laptop window (1512 px wide; gaps 16 px, margins 24 px). No h means the Tile is as tall as its Panel or Note, at most about two-thirds of the user's window height (a taller Panel scrolls inside it). With h, a Panel's Tile is that tall where its Panel is taller, and its Panel scrolls inside it; h beyond its Panel's own height is capped at that height, and the Fit report says so (capped). With h, a Note's Tile is that tall, even taller than its text. Only the listed Tiles move. Tiles float up: y orders them, and each sits right under whatever is above it in its columns; a Tile placed on others pushes them, and those under them, down, hidden Tiles too. x + w over 12, or a negative or zero value, is refused with the reason, and then nothing moves; so is a Tile you can't see. A width below a Panel's minimum is taken, and the Panel shows scaled. Returns every Tile's placement. Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, have an h taller than their Panel (capped, with the h they got), scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.
name: arrange
